newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends with heavy feel on day's lows.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends with heavy feel on day's lows.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed on its lows and with a heavy feel on Wednesday after merchandise trade data, comments from Treasurer Winston Peters and the Fed rate rise all failed to excite.
The currency finished at US$0.6920/30 and 68.34 on its Trade-Weighted Index, down from 0.6933/40 and 68.50 at the opening.

Dealers said the quarter point rate rise by the Federal Open Market Committee was already factored into currency markets and news of a NZ$159.7 million merchandise trade surplus in February had no impact on the Kiwi.
There was only a brief move down on comments from Peters that exporters should take heart from the Reserve Bank's view that the New Zealand dollar's rise may have peaked.
A dealer said the Kiwi was in no man's land, with corporate buyers waiting between 0.6880 and 0.6910, and sellers having done their business earlier in the week up at 0.6960.

A softer Australian dollar was also weighing on Kiwi and in the absence of other factors was likely to continue to set the direction. Another dealer saw the Kiwi as "toppish" around 0.6950 and favoured a move down towards 0.6900.
